QUOTE: ".yaml`, `.yml`, `.json` | yes | no, by design | no" and "`.yaml` or `.sh` file gets its `path` row on any install. A YAML file is 'findable by name' and that is all." and "Their grammars only offer `block_mapping_pair` and `pair`. Writing those as `memberdef` rows would put every `steps:` key into the namespace"
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer says YAML/JSON files are registered in the file set (path row) but have no symbols by design, in contrast to shell/CMake which get definitions.
